scenes.title: Soda & dbt Tests for Quality
scenes.subtitle: Declarative checks inside your stack
scenes.narration: Soda and dbt let you express data quality checks as configuration that runs alongside your transformations.

scenes.heading: Soda versus dbt tests

right.heading: dbt tests
points: Runs as part of dbt build
Great for schema and relationship tests

scenes.narration: Soda expresses checks in a dedicated YAML language and can run independently against many warehouses, with strong support for freshness and anomaly detection. dbt tests live right next to the models they validate and execute as part of a dbt build. Many teams use dbt tests for structural rules and Soda for broader monitoring.

scenes.heading: Common test types
bullets: not_null and unique on key columns
custom thresholds on freshness and volume
scenes.narration: The not-null and unique tests guard the integrity of primary keys. Accepted-values tests keep categorical columns within their allowed domain, and relationship tests confirm foreign keys reference existing parent rows. Custom thresholds extend this to freshness and volume expectations.

scenes.heading: dbt schema tests
scenes.code:
models:
  - name: orders
    columns:
      - name: order_id
        tests:
          - not_null
          - unique
      - name: status
        tests:
          - accepted_values:
              values: ['new', 'paid', 'shipped']
      - name: customer_id
        tests:
          - relationships:
              to: ref('customers')
              field: customer_id
scenes.narration: This dbt schema file attaches tests declaratively to the columns of the orders model. The order identifier must be both non-null and unique, enforcing a valid primary key. The status column is constrained to a known set of values, and the customer identifier must reference an existing row in the customers model.

scenes.text: Declarative checks live with your code, run in CI, and fail the build before bad data reaches consumers.
scenes.narration: By expressing quality as configuration next to your transformations, tests stay in sync with the models they protect. Running them in your pipeline turns quality into an automatic gate rather than a manual review.
